MAT-02.reason: Either answer to P versus NP has different consequences; a resolution alone need not provide a practical solver. No unconditional capability arrow is justified.

MAT-03.reason: Existence and regularity of 3D solutions do not themselves supply a fast numerical solver or turbulence control. A concrete computational mechanism is missing.

MAT-04.reason: No target in this collection specifies an algorithm or device whose construction follows from the stated algebraic-cycle result.

MAT-05.reason: The rank/L-function identity alone does not supply a concrete capability in the collection; a constructive downstream method is unspecified.

MAT-06.reason: Existence and a mass gap do not directly provide a usable chemistry or engineering model. No specific application mechanism is established by the source.

MAT-07.reason: The integer iteration conjecture has no described engineering or scientific target in the collection that would be enabled by its resolution.

MAT-08.reason: The prime-sum existence statement supplies no specified constructive capability or prerequisite for another listed milestone.

MAT-09.reason: Infinitely many prime pairs do not directly supply the secure primitives listed here; a number-theory-to-cryptography arrow would be speculative without a construction.

MAT-10.reason: A perfect-number existence result has no concrete downstream capability specified in these source entries.

CSC-01.reason: Source explicitly flags equivalence to MAT-02. Retain that metadata; a duplicate is not a causal prerequisite.

CSC-02.reason: A one-way-function construction alone does not establish the advanced primitives, quantum security or efficiency targets here. A suitable reduction and adversary model are unspecified.

CSC-05.reason: Fast matrix multiplication has broad possible uses, but no listed target provides a specific bottleneck and end-to-end improvement argument. A generic faster-compute arrow was rejected.

CSC-06.reason: An approximation-hardness resolution does not itself provide the efficient capabilities listed here; no justified constructive pathway was identified.

CSC-07.reason: A statement about physical simulation limits is not a new computational device or algorithm. No concrete capability direction is justified without the theorem’s outcome.

CRY-02.reason: No listed implementation platform or hardness construction establishes the simultaneous security, key-size and speed target; related signature goals overlap rather than cause it.

CRY-06.reason: This is a specialized post-quantum signature ambition. The broader public-key ambition is overlapping scope, not a demonstrated enabling mechanism.

QUA-01.reason: Source flags equivalence to CSC-04. Keep its original entry and canonical reference, not a causal arrow between equivalent goals.

QUA-10.reason: The desired new computational model is unspecified; naming algorithm families does not justify a directional link to a particular unproved speedup.
